What a bot-traffic audit of our launch day actually found

We pulled the raw access log from launch day and ran it through a simple audit instead of trusting the dashboard number. The dashboard said ten thousand visits. The log told a different story: a large share of the requests came from clients whose user-agent plainly declared a crawler, and another slice never pulled a single stylesheet or image, which is what a real browser does when a person loads a page.

Once we removed the declared bots and the render-nothing hits, the human figure was a fraction of the headline. That changed how we read the whole launch: the channel we thought worked had mostly sent machines, and the one small forum post we almost ignored had sent the humans who actually stayed and clicked through.

Here is the method we used, the thresholds we picked, and why, so you can run the same check on your own log and stop trusting a number you have not taken apart. If this is useful you can follow along where I write these up.
